gotchas: DIALECT UNKNOWN, AND THE OBVIOUS ASSIGNMENT IS REFUTED. The tempting move is to file the 130PW under the wall-battery dialect: same vendor, same PW suffix, same 51.2 V. The vendor's own wall-battery manual V2.7 names its covered models on the cover page — 52, 100, 156, 174, 200, 280 and 300PW. 130 is not among them. No
What the datasheet DOES give is a bare list of physical interfaces. No baud rate, no protocol name, no default, no DIP range, no pinout, no map. A driver cannot be started from it.

The 130PW also differs from the manual's models in a way that matters: 'Up to 32 units in parallel', where the wall manual's DIP table runs to 63 and the rack line claims 40 or 63. A different parallel ceiling suggests a different BMS generation, which is exactly what would fork the map.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a BSLBATT manual whose cover page includes 130PW, or a second BSLBATT document showing the 130PW's protocol-selection menu. Either would move this to vendor-doc in an afternoon. Until then it stays unknown — the 130PW is a Tier C model with no dialect, not a wall-dialect model.
